title: Release 0.2.0
description:
## Summary

- Bumps the package version to `0.2.0`.
- Adds the `0.2.0` changelog section with the approved release notes.
- Removes the stale direct `griffe<2.0` dev dependency so CI can resolve the current `great-docs` git dependency.

## Public Facing Changes

- Documents the main `0.2.0` additions: crawl and ingest APIs, crawler caching, `CloudflareCrawler`, `PostgreSQLStore`, and `EmbeddingNVIDIA`.
- Calls out the compatibility note for `CrawlScope.include_patterns` and `CrawlScope.exclude_patterns`: string patterns now use one glob-style syntax across crawlers, and regex behavior requires compiled `re.Pattern` objects.

## Internal Changes

- Drops a stale dev-only `griffe` constraint. `great-docs` now supplies its compatible `griffe` dependency.

## Testing

- `uv sync --all-extras`
- `uv sync --all-extras --refresh-package great-docs`
- `./.venv/bin/task format`
- `./.venv/bin/task format_check`
- `./.venv/bin/task lint_check`
- `./.venv/bin/task tests`
- `./.venv/bin/task docs_build`

`./.venv/bin/task check` and standalone `./.venv/bin/task types_check` were interrupted because the local `pyright` process produced no diagnostics and did not complete after several minutes.

title: docs: add more coverage on docstring content
description: This PR expands and clarifies the API reference docstrings across the chunk, document, chunker, embedding-protocol, and utility modules. I added quite a few descriptions (that were missing), and text around examples (explaining the example code). It also resolves the duplicated "Parameter Attributes" / "Attributes" sections on dataclass pages by documenting fields under a single `Parameters` section. There were two broken chonkie links (now fixed).

description:
This PR restructures the User Guide into four progressive sections (Get Started, Building a Store, Using Your Store, and Storage Backends) by renumbering the source files (no changes to any published URLs). Adds two new Get Started pages:

1. a "Why raghilda?" positioning page
2. a runnable, no-API-key Quickstart

The PR also polishes the README and provides a fuller footer (Requirements, Links, Contributing, License, etc.).

description: This PR fixes three small documentation issues in raghilda: a broken "examples" link in the Getting Started guide that pointed at the project's old `dfalbel/py-ragnar` repo, and a duplicate PyPI link on the landing page caused by a redundant `[project.urls]` entry. It also sets `site_url` in `great-docs.yml`, which populates the canonical documentation address so the auto-generated Skills page renders working install commands instead of showing a literal `<site-url>/skill.md` placeholder in the manual/curl option.

title: enh: unify `CrawlScope` pattern API on glob syntax
description:
This PR unifies how `CrawlScope`'s `include_patterns` and `exclude_patterns` are interpreted. It now provides a single glob syntax (`*` for one path segment, `**` for any number of segments) that works identically across `WebCrawler`, `DirectoryCrawler`, and `CloudflareCrawler`.

Before the web/directory crawlers treated patterns as regexes while Cloudflare used globs. This wasn't ideal as it would force users to rewrite patterns when switching backends. The strategy here is to have globs converted to regexes under the hood for local matching, while Cloudflare still receives them directly (so, standardizing on Cloudflare's patterns).

For matching that globs can't express, you can now pass a pre-compiled `re.Pattern` (matched with `re.search`) anywhere a string is accepted. You can even freely mix the two in one list. For Cloudflare, these regexes are applied client-side to returned records since the API can't evaluate them.

Important to note here that this is a change for existing `WebCrawler`/`DirectoryCrawler` users who passed regex strings. Those now must now be globs or wrapped in `re.compile(...)`.

Fixes: https://github.com/posit-dev/raghilda/issues/79

title: docs: add chatlas integration and `CloudflareCrawler` user guide articles
description:
This PR adds two user guide pages: (1) `05-chatlas-integration.qmd` and (2) `52-cloudflare-crawler.qmd`.

The first covers how to integrate raghilda's RAG capabilities with the chatlas package, including connecting to a knowledge store, defining and registering retrieval tools for LLMs, tailoring retrieval logic, and working with different model providers.

The second guide page documents the `CloudflareCrawler` for building stores from JavaScript-rendered sites via Cloudflare's Browser Rendering API. The guide covers credentials setup, browser rendering controls, page discovery options, Cloudflare-style filtering patterns, caching, incremental updates with `modified_since=`, polling configuration, and lower-level inspection methods. A full example script demonstrates both initial builds and incremental refreshes.

title: Clarify DuckDB BM25 index lifecycle
description:
## User Facing Changes

- Update the README quickstart example to include the required `store.build_index()` call.

- `retrieve()` and `retrieve_bm25()` with a DuckDB store now raise a clearer error when retrieval is called before the BM25 index has been built, or after writes have made the BM25 index stale.

For example, this now fails with an actionable error:

```python
from raghilda.store import DuckDBStore

store = DuckDBStore.create("raghilda.db", embed=None)

# ... upsert chunked documents ...

store.retrieve_bm25("query", top_k=5)
```

```text
RuntimeError: DuckDBStore retrieval requires a current BM25 index. Call `store.build_index("bm25")` after inserting or updating documents and before calling `retrieve_bm25()` or `retrieve()`.
```

## Internal Changes

- Track BM25 freshness in DuckDB store metadata with `bm25_index_is_current`.
- Mark BM25 stale after `upsert()`.
- Mark BM25 current after `build_index("bm25")`.
- Restore BM25 state on reconnect without adding a metadata query to the retrieval hot path.
- Keep legacy stores backward-compatible by trusting an existing DuckDB FTS index when the new metadata column is missing.
- Leave HNSW behavior unchanged because DuckDB maintains HNSW indexes across writes, while DuckDB FTS/BM25 requires rebuilding.

BM25 freshness is tracked per store handle. The implementation intentionally avoids re-reading metadata on every retrieval; multiple live `DuckDBStore` handles pointing at the same database file are unsupported.

Closes https://github.com/posit-dev/raghilda/issues/74

title: Introduce cached, concurrent crawl and ingest APIs
description:
## Summary

The primary motivation for this PR is to make store creation workflows faster
in practice.

Raghilda can make store creation faster in two ways:

- local caching to avoid repeated fetches and repeated conversion work across runs
  (and make interrupted store creation jobs resumable)
- concurrency to do more crawl and ingest work in parallel within a run

This PR introduces a crawl and ingest API that makes caching and concurrency
available in a principled way, without forcing everything into one opaque
pipeline.

The design centers on a visible seam between crawler and store:

```python
crawler.markdown_documents(scope) -> Iterator[MarkdownDocument]
store.ingest(documents, prepare=None, max_workers=1) -> IngestSummary
```

That seam matters because it lets us add caching and concurrency while keeping
the workflow inspectable and composable:

- callers can inspect discovered origins
- callers can fetch or convert one origin directly
- callers can chunk outside the crawler
- callers can rerun ingest policy without re-fetching content
- callers are not forced into one monolithic, opaque, `run(..., store=...)` path

The crawl side is centered on:

```python
crawler.markdown_documents(scope) -> Iterator[MarkdownDocument]
```

The ingest side is centered on:

```python
store.ingest(documents, prepare=None, max_workers=1) -> IngestSummary
store.upsert(document) -> WriteResult
```

This PR covers both pieces because the crawler/store seam is best described in
terms of the document objects moving through the pipeline.

## Proposed Crawler Contract

The main happy path is:

```python
crawler.markdown_documents(scope) -> Iterator[MarkdownDocument]
```

Additional lower-level crawler methods are also part of the API:

- `origins(scope) -> Iterator[str]`
- `fetch_raw(origin, cache_force_refresh=False) -> FetchedSource`
- `fetch_markdown(origin, cache_force_refresh=False) -> MarkdownDocument`

`BaseCrawler` defines this contract and is exposed for subclassing.

## `CrawlScope`

`CrawlScope` owns the traversal policy definition.

```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class CrawlScope:
    roots: str | Path | Sequence[str | Path]
    include_patterns: Sequence[str] | None = None
    exclude_patterns: Sequence[str] | None = None
    depth: int | None = None
    limit: int | None = None
    include_types: Sequence[str] | None = None
    exclude_types: Sequence[str] | None = None
    include_external_links: bool = False
    include_subdomains: bool = False
```

The split is:

- `CrawlScope` defines what to crawl for one run
- the crawler constructor configures backend-specific behavior

## `FetchedSource`

One shared intermediate across crawler implementations is `FetchedSource`.

```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class FetchedSource:
    origin: str
    body_path: Path
    resolved_origin: str | None = None
    content_type: str | None = None
    status_code: int | None = None
    metadata: dict[str, Any] | None = None
    fetched_at: datetime | None = None
    revalidated_at: datetime | None = None
    markdown_path: Path | None = None
```

It is the inspectable boundary that abstracts away whether an origin is
resolved via an actual web call or from the local filesystem cache.

## Concrete Crawlers

Raghilda exposes:

- `DirectoryCrawler`
- `WebCrawler`
- `CloudflareCrawler`

Constructors stay backend-specific:

```python
DirectoryCrawler(
    *,
    cache_dir: bool | str | Path | None = None,
    max_workers: int = 1,
)

WebCrawler(
    *,
    session: requests.Session | None = None,
    cache_dir: bool | str | Path | None = None,
    cache_stale_after: timedelta | None = None,
    max_workers: int = 1,
)

CloudflareCrawler(
    *,
    account_id: str,
    api_token: str,
    cache_dir: bool | str | Path | None = None,
    session: requests.Session | Any | None = None,
    source: str = "all",
    render: bool = True,
    cache_stale_after: timedelta | None = None,
    modified_since: int | None = None,
    poll_interval: float = 5.0,
    max_poll_attempts: int = 60,
    max_workers: int = 1,
    base_url: str = "https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4",
)
```

Cache-related controls use a `cache_` prefix:

- `cache_dir=`
- `cache_stale_after=`
- `cache_force_refresh=`

## Concurrency

This PR includes concurrency on both sides of the seam, with independent
threadpools used by the crawler and the store writer.

### Crawl-Side Concurrency

- `markdown_documents()` can fetch and convert concurrently
- `WebCrawler.origins()` can fetch a breadth-first frontier concurrently while
  preserving stable output order; `markdown_documents()` preserves the same
  order as `origins()`
- callers still have direct access to `origins()`, `fetch_raw()`, and
  `fetch_markdown()`

### Store-Side Concurrency

- `store.ingest(..., max_workers=..., prepare=...)` can perform concurrent
  writes while continuing to prepare later documents as the stream is consumed

## Caching

This PR adds an internal filesystem cache, but does not introduce a public
cache abstraction yet. It is intentionally a flat directory of files so it
stays easy to inspect with normal file tools.

The cache layout is:

```text
<root>/<sanitized-key>--<hash>.metadata.json
<root>/<sanitized-key>--<hash><ext>
```

If `cache_dir=True`, the cache resolves to a backend-specific directory under:

```text
.raghilda/cache/directory
.raghilda/cache/web
.raghilda/cache/cloudflare
```

The metadata sidecar is the source of truth for each cache entry.

This cache is also part of the practical interruptibility story. The persistent
crawl cache plus the store's own upsert behavior act as an ad hoc resumability
mechanism: if a script is interrupted and rerun without underlying content
changes, the rerun should stay cheap enough in practice without exposing a
large public state object that can drift out of sync.

## Store Seam

The crawler/store seam is:

- crawler methods produce `MarkdownDocument`
- optional preparation converts documents into the shape a store wants
- `upsert()` writes the final store-specific document shape

That keeps chunking outside the crawler.

Store expectations differ:

- `DuckDBStore.upsert()` expects `ChunkedMarkdownDocument`
- `ChromaDBStore.upsert()` expects `ChunkedMarkdownDocument`
- `PostgreSQLStore.upsert()` expects `ChunkedMarkdownDocument`
- `OpenAIStore.upsert()` expects `MarkdownDocument`

## Ingest API

The convenience path is:

```python
store.ingest(documents, prepare=None, max_workers=1) -> IngestSummary
```

The lower-level path is:

```python
store.upsert(document) -> WriteResult
```

The intended behavior is:

- inputs are consumed lazily
- `prepare` is applied as documents are read from the input iterable
- writes are submitted incrementally to a threadpool
- duplicate-origin detection is best effort over a bounded recent window
- a duplicate raises `ValueError` when encountered
- no rollback is attempted
- already running writes are allowed to complete before the error is surfaced
- rerunning after interruption should still be cheap in practice when crawl cache hits and store upserts can avoid unnecessary work

This keeps ingest streaming while still catching nearby duplicate-origin
mistakes.

## Example

```python
from raghilda.chunker import MarkdownChunker
from raghilda.crawl import CrawlScope, WebCrawler
from raghilda.store import DuckDBStore

crawler = WebCrawler(cache_dir=".cache/crawl", max_workers=4)

scope = CrawlScope(
    roots=["https://example.com/docs"],
    include_patterns=["https://example.com/docs/**"],
    depth=2,
)

documents = crawler.markdown_documents(scope)

store = DuckDBStore.create(
    location="raghilda.duckdb",
    overwrite=True,
    embed=None,
)

summary = store.ingest(
    documents,
    prepare=MarkdownChunker(chunk_size=1000).chunk,
    max_workers=4,
)
```

For `OpenAIStore`, there is no chunking step:

```python
documents = crawler.markdown_documents(scope)
store.ingest(documents)
```

## Non-Goals

This PR does not try to settle:

- a public cache abstraction
- a public `crawler.cache` object
- a top-level `crawler.run(..., store=...)` wrapper
- the full long-term ingest API beyond `ingest()` and `upsert()`
- a generic crawler plugin system

## Open Questions

- Is `markdown_documents()` the right main happy path?
- Is `CrawlScope` the right name?
- How much cache control should be public now beyond `cache_dir=`,
  `cache_stale_after=`, and `cache_force_refresh=`?
- Should converted-document caching stay internal?
- Is the current crawler/store seam sufficient, or do we need a thinner or
  thicker convenience layer on top later?

title: Add PostgreSQL store backed by psycopg2 and pgvector
description:
## Summary
- Adds `PostgreSQLStore` backed by psycopg2 and pgvector
- Full CRUD support: `create`, `connect`, `upsert`, `retrieve`, `size`
- **Full-text search** via `retrieve_fts` using PostgreSQL's `tsvector`/`tsquery` with a pre-computed column and GIN index
- **Vector similarity search** via `retrieve_vss` using pgvector with HNSW indexes (cosine, L2, inner product)
- **Combined retrieval** via `retrieve` merging VSS + FTS results with deoverlap support
- Attribute support: scalar types, float vectors, and struct types (mapped to JSONB)
- `build_index` method for adding VSS indexes after creation
- `vss_index` parameter in `create` to control default index type
- Dev script (`scripts/postgres-dev.sh`) to launch a local PostgreSQL+pgvector Docker container
- pgvector service container added to CI

## Test plan
- 23 tests covering create, connect, upsert, retrieve (FTS + VSS + combined), size, and attribute edge cases
- Tests run against a real PostgreSQL+pgvector instance (Docker in CI, local via dev script)

title: Add PostgreSQL backend with pgvector support
description:
## Summary

- Adds a `PostgresStore` backend using pgvector for vector similarity search and PostgreSQL's built-in tsvector/tsquery for full-text search
- Each store uses a separate PostgreSQL database for isolation
- Extracts shared helpers from `DuckDBStore` into `_store_helpers.py` for code reuse (no DuckDB behavior changes)
- Adds PostgreSQL as a GitHub Actions service container for CI

## Key changes

- **`_postgres_store.py`**: Full `PostgresStore` implementation with `create()`, `connect()`, `upsert()`, `retrieve()`, `retrieve_vss()`, `retrieve_fts()`, `build_index()`, and `size()`
- **`_store_helpers.py`**: Shared validation, chunk classes, SQL utilities extracted from DuckDB backend
- **`_attribute_schema.py`**: `postgres_sql_type_for_attribute_type()` mapping (TEXT, vector(N), JSONB, etc.)
- **`_attribute_filters.py`**: `compile_filter_to_sql_postgres()` with JSONB `->>`/`->` path access
- **`docker-compose.yml`**: pgvector/pgvector:pg17 container for local testing
- **CI**: PostgreSQL service added to `check.yml` workflow

title: Refactor chunking around explicit chunked document types
description:
## Summary

This refactor makes chunked documents an explicit part of the API instead of storing optional chunk state on `Document` / `MarkdownDocument`.

### What changed

- add `ChunkedDocument` and `ChunkedMarkdownDocument` as first-class document types
- add `Document.to_chunked(...)` / `MarkdownDocument.to_chunked(...)` for attaching precomputed chunks
- change chunker behavior so `chunker.chunk(document)` returns a chunked document without mutating the input document
- reserve `chunker.chunk_text(text)` for raw text-to-chunks use cases
- tighten protocol boundaries with `ChunkedDocumentLike` and stricter `from_any()` conversions
- update DuckDB and Chroma stores to require explicit chunked markdown documents for upsert paths
- keep OpenAI store limited to unchunked markdown documents
- make `WriteResult` generic so store writes preserve the concrete document type they return
- update examples, docs, and compatibility tests to use the new chunking flow

## Why

This makes the API more explicit and less error-prone:

- unchunked and chunked document states are now distinct types
- chunking no longer mutates input documents in place
- store APIs can validate more clearly whether they expect chunked or unchunked inputs
- integrations like chonkie can target the right protocol directly

## Breaking changes

- `Document` and `MarkdownDocument` no longer carry a mutable `.chunks` field
- `chunker.chunk_document(doc)` becomes `chunker.chunk(doc)`
- `chunker.chunk(text)` becomes `chunker.chunk_text(text)`
- code that previously built chunked documents by assigning `.chunks` should now use `.to_chunked(...)`
- code converting chunked external objects should use `ChunkedDocument.from_any(...)`

## Testing

- updated API contract, document, chunker, store, Chroma, and chonkie compatibility tests
- docs/examples updated to reflect the new public API

title: Remove ingest() from public store API
description:
## Summary

This removes `ingest()` from the public store API ahead of the initial public release.

`ingest()` looked like a small convenience, but it sits at the seam between content acquisition and indexing. As soon as we want to support
resumable local caching, alternative crawl backends such as Cloudflare `/crawl`, and configurable bulk orchestration, it stops being “just batch
upsert” and starts locking in much larger API decisions. For now the supported workflow remains explicit:

1. Read content into a document
2. Chunk the document
3. Call `store.upsert()`

## Changes

- Removed `ingest()` from `DuckDBStore`
- Removed `ingest()` from `ChromaDBStore`
- Deleted the internal lazy threaded mapping helper used by ingest
- Updated API contract tests to assert `ingest()` is not exposed
- Removed ingest-specific tests
- Rewrote README, examples, and user guide snippets to use explicit
  `read_as_markdown()` -> `chunk_document()` -> `upsert()` steps

## Why

Bulk ingestion is where several still-evolving concerns meet:

- where crawling ends and store ingestion begins
- what the extension point should be for acquisition backends, including local crawling, cached crawling, and Cloudflare `/crawl`
- how cache and resume state should be represented so interrupted runs do not repeat work
- how concurrency, progress, cancellation, and error handling should interact with cached and partially completed work
- which defaults belong to stores versus higher-level orchestration

Those are all design questions we are actively iterating on, and they will likely land as a separate series of PRs. Removing `ingest()` now
avoids freezing an underdesigned orchestration API into the public store surface before that work is ready.

## Validation

- `./.venv/bin/task check`
- `./.venv/bin/task tests`
- `./.venv/bin/task docs_build`

All passed locally.

## Notes

This does not remove `upsert()` or its existing `skip_if_unchanged` behavior. It only removes the higher-level bulk ingestion entry point so that
crawling, caching, concurrency, and bulk indexing can be redesigned separately.

title: fix: serialize markitdown patching in read_as_markdown
description:
## Summary

This PR fixes the intermittent `read_as_markdown()` flake caused by concurrent tests patching `markitdown`'s global markdown converter methods at the same time.

## What changed

- serialize `_patched_markitdown` with a module-level lock in `read.py`
- restore the patched converter methods under `try/finally` so the lock is always released cleanly
- add a regression test that proves a second thread cannot enter the global patch while the first is still active

## Why this fixes the flake

`_patched_markitdown` temporarily replaces `_CustomMarkdownify.convert_soup` and `_CustomMarkdownify.convert_pre`, which are process-global. Without synchronization, concurrent calls to `read_as_markdown()` can interleave those mutations and leave later calls observing the wrong selector behavior.

Serializing the patch window makes those temporary global overrides safe.

## Tests

Passed:
- `./.venv/bin/pytest tests/test_read.py::test_patched_markitdown_serializes_global_converter_patches -q`
- `./.venv/bin/pytest tests/test_read.py -q`
- `./.venv/bin/task check`
- `./.venv/bin/task tests`

title: refactor: move ingest orchestration into a shared API
description:
## Summary

This PR moves ingest orchestration out of store classes and into a shared `raghilda.ingest` API.

It adds:
- `ingest(...)`
- `Ingestor`
- `IngestResults`
- `ItemOutcome`
- `ItemError`

It also removes store-level `ingest()` methods so stores stay focused on persistence.

## API changes

- Added `raghilda.ingest`
- Added `BaseStore.default_prepare()`
- `BaseStore.default_prepare()` now uses `read_as_markdown()` + `MarkdownChunker`
- `OpenAIStore.default_prepare()` now uses `read_as_markdown()` without chunking
- Removed `DuckDBStore.ingest()`
- Removed `ChromaDBStore.ingest()`

## Behavior

- Shared ingest now returns itemized results via `IngestResults`
- Aggregate counts (`inserted`, `replaced`, `skipped`, `cancelled`, `failed`, `pending`) are derived from per-item outcomes
- `on_error="skip"` records per-item failures and continues
- `on_error="raise"` stops submitting new items after the first failure, drains already-submitted work, and raises `ItemError` with `partial_results`
- OpenAI managed uploads now normalize filenames instead of leaking local paths into uploaded names

## Docs and examples

README, examples, and user guide pages now use:

```python
from raghilda.ingest import ingest

results = ingest(paths, store=store)
print(results.inserted, results.replaced, results.failed)
```

## Tests

This replaces store-specific ingest tests with shared ingest coverage for:
- list input
- generator input with bounded lazy consumption
- custom `prepare`
- inserted / replaced / skipped aggregation
- `on_error="raise"`
- `on_error="skip"`

description:

- If `chunk.origin` already matches `document.origin`, behavior is unchanged.

## Internal-only changes

- Added `_validate_chunk_origin_matches_document_origin(...)` helper.
- Existing chunk text consistency validation remains in place.

title: fix(chroma): serialize collection access to prevent telemetry race
description:
## Summary

- Existing locks (`_origin_lock`, `_chunk_id_lock`) are preserved as they protect different invariants (read-modify-write sequences and ID allocation, respectively)

title: refactor(store): replace `insert()` with origin-keyed `upsert()` and WriteResult
description:
## Summary

This PR redesigns and renames the main single-document write action from `insert()` to `upsert()`.

The goal is to support efficient in-place store updates by re-running the same document creation pipeline without blindly rewriting unchanged content.

What started as a smaller change expanded as API design issues surfaced during implementation and  discussions over slack. The result is a tighter write contract and a clearer identity model across backends.

## Key API Design Decisions

- Removed public `doc_id` from the API surface.
- Renamed `Document.id` to `origin`.
- `origin` is now the user-provided unique key required for upsert flows.
- Added `chunk_ids` to `RetrievedChunk` to support filters that exclude already-seen chunks.
- Added a new `WriteResult` return type for single-document writes.

## New Write Contract

`upsert(document, skip_if_unchanged=True) -> WriteResult`

`WriteResult` includes:
- `action`: `inserted | replaced | skipped`
- `document`: current persisted snapshot
- `replaced_document`: previous snapshot when a replacement occurs

This enables deterministic write outcomes and explicit handling of no-op writes.

## User-Facing Changes

- `insert()` usage is replaced by `upsert()` across stores and docs.
- Callers are now required to provide stable `origin` values for document identity.
- Retrieval outputs now carry `chunk_ids`, enabling usage of “seen chunk” exclusion patterns in attribute filters.

## Internal Changes

- Backends were aligned to the same upsert semantics and result contract.
- Skip-if-unchanged logic was tightened to avoid unnecessary rewrite/re-embed work.
- Snapshot/replacement paths were hardened for consistency and failure handling.
- Tests were expanded to lock the new API contract and update behavior.

title: Fix DuckDB cursor thread safety issue causing commit() to hang
description:
## Summary

- Fixes thread safety issues with DuckDB connection access
- Adds `_db_lock` to serialize all database operations (reads and writes)
- Uses the connection directly instead of creating cursors
- Keeps embedding operations outside the lock for parallelism

## Problem

When using `store.ingest()` with `ThreadPoolExecutor`, DuckDB operations could hang or behave unpredictably because DuckDB connections are not thread-safe.

## Root Cause

DuckDB connections should not be accessed concurrently from multiple threads. The previous implementation:
1. Created cursors in worker threads which could hang on `commit()`
2. Had no synchronization for read operations (`retrieve_vss`, `retrieve_bm25`)

## Solution

According to the [DuckDB documentation on multiple threads](https://duckdb.org/docs/stable/guides/python/multiple_threads), it is technically possible to use DuckDB from multiple threads by creating separate cursors per thread. However, this approach complicates the implementation and we encountered hangs on `commit()` when cursors were created in worker threads.

Instead, we use a simpler approach with a lock to serialize all DB operations:

1. Add a `_db_lock` (threading.Lock) to serialize all DB operations
2. Use the connection directly (`self.con.execute()`) instead of creating cursors
3. Apply the lock to both writes and reads
4. Keep embedding operations (external API calls) outside the lock for parallelism

```python
# Write operations
with self._db_lock:
    self.con.begin()
    _duckdb_append(self.con, "documents", doc)
    _duckdb_append(self.con, "embeddings", chunks)
    self.con.commit()

# Read operations
with self._db_lock:
    result = self.con.execute(sql)
    rows = result.fetchall()
```

---

This is a port of #27 to the current main branch after recent refactoring.

title: Add cross-backend support for document attributes and retrieval filters
description:
## Intent
This PR adds a unified `attributes` API across stores and retrieval-time filtering via `attributes_filter`.

Users can now:
1. Define typed attribute schemas at store creation.
2. Attach attributes at insert time (document-level, and chunk-level where supported).
3. Restrict retrieval candidates using a shared filter syntax across backends.

It also tightens up terminology to be explicit and consistent:
- `attributes`: user-defined fields for retrieval scoping.
- `metadata`: store/resource-level backend metadata.

See `examples/metadata_filters.py` for an end-to-end example.

## API highlights
```python
from typing import Annotated
from raghilda.store import DuckDBStore

store = DuckDBStore.create(
    location=":memory:",
    embed=None,
    attributes={  # NEW
        "tenant": str,                  # required
        "priority": (int, 0),           # optional default
        "is_public": (bool, False),     # optional default
        "topic": (str | None, None),    # optional nullable default
        "embedding25": Annotated[list[float], 25],  # DuckDB-only vector attribute
    },
)

store.insert(doc, attributes={"tenant": "docs"})

chunks = store.retrieve(
    "beta",
    top_k=5,
    attributes_filter="tenant = 'docs' AND priority >= 5", # NEW
)
```

`attributes_filter` accepts:
1. SQL-like strings (`=`, `!=`, `>`, `>=`, `<`, `<=`, `IN`, `NOT IN`, `AND`, `OR`, parentheses, plus `IS NULL` / `IS NOT NULL` where supported).
2. Dict AST form (`{"type": "...", "filters": [...]}` with comparison nodes using `key` + `value`).


Example translation of:

```python
attributes_filter = "tenant = 'docs' AND priority >= 5 AND topic IN ('guide', 'reference')"
``` 
to the dict form:
```python
attributes_filter = {
    "type": "and",
    "filters": [
        {"type": "eq", "key": "tenant", "value": "docs"},
        {"type": "gte", "key": "priority", "value": 5},
        {"type": "in", "key": "topic", "value": ["guide", "reference"]},
    ],
}
```
## What changed
1. Added centralized schema/filter logic in `src/raghilda/_metadata.py`.
2. Added typed attribute schemas from dicts and class annotations.
3. Added inline `(type, default)` schema declarations.
4. Added optional scalar support (`T | None`) for DuckDB schemas.
5. Added DuckDB vector attributes via `Annotated[list[float], N]`.
6. Added backend-specific filter compilation:
   - DuckDB SQL `WHERE`
   - Chroma `where`
   - OpenAI `filters`
7. Extended `DuckDBStore`, `ChromaDBStore`, and `OpenAIStore` for:
   - `attributes` schema at create/connect
   - `insert(..., attributes=...)`
   - `retrieve(..., attributes_filter=...)`
8. Added schema/spec serialization + restoration in persisted metadata.
9. Added tests:
   - `tests/test_metadata_filter.py`
   - `tests/test_metadata_schema.py`
   - `tests/test_openai_store_metadata.py`
   - expanded integration coverage in `tests/test_store.py` and `tests/test_chroma_store.py`
10. Added docs in `user_guide/03-metadata-filters.qmd` and example in `examples/metadata_filters.py`.

## Backend behavior
1. DuckDB: scalar + fixed-size vector attributes.
2. DuckDB: required and optional/defaulted attributes supported.
3. ChromaDB/OpenAI: scalar attributes only.
4. ChromaDB/OpenAI: declared attributes must be required (no optional/defaulted schema fields).
5. ChromaDB/OpenAI: `NULL` filters rejected.
6. Null comparisons use `IS NULL` / `IS NOT NULL`; `= NULL` / `!= NULL` are rejected.
7. Non-equality null comparisons (`> NULL`, `>= NULL`, `< NULL`, `<= NULL`) raise `ValueError`.
8. OpenAIStore rejects per-chunk attributes (document-level attributes only).

## Validation
- `./.venv/bin/task format_check` ✅  
- `./.venv/bin/task lint_check` ✅  
- `./.venv/bin/task tests` ✅  
- `./.venv/bin/task docs_build` ✅  
- `./.venv/bin/task types_check` ✅

title: Make ingest() stream items lazily instead of materializing entire iterator
description:
## Summary
- Add shared `lazy_map()` utility in `_utils.py`
- Update `DuckDBStore.ingest()` and `ChromaDBStore.ingest()` to use it

## Problem
`ThreadPoolExecutor.map()` eagerly consumes the entire iterator upfront to submit all tasks. When ingesting from generators (e.g., streaming from GitHub API), this caused memory issues and defeated the purpose of using generators.

## Solution
Added `lazy_map()` which:
- Only keeps `max_workers` tasks in flight at a time
- Pulls new items from the iterator as workers become available
- Yields futures as they complete (results may be out of order, which is fine for ingest)

This keeps memory usage constant regardless of iterator size.

## Changes
- `src/raghilda/_utils.py` - New shared utility module with `lazy_map()`
- `src/raghilda/_store.py` - DuckDBStore uses `lazy_map()`
- `src/raghilda/_chroma_store.py` - ChromaDBStore uses `lazy_map()`

title: Reorganize module structure for better type organization
description:
## Summary

- Create dedicated `chunk` module with Chunk, MarkdownChunk, RetrievedChunk, Metric
- Create dedicated `embedding` module with EmbeddingProvider, EmbeddingOpenAI
- Move Document and MarkdownDocument definitions to `document` module
- Move BaseChunker to `_chunker` module alongside RaghildaMarkdownChunker
- Rename Store to BaseStore for consistency with BaseChunker
- Simplify `_types` module to only contain protocol definitions
- Update `types` module to export only protocol types
- Update all cross-module imports to use public modules instead of internal ones

## New module structure

| Module | Contents |
|--------|----------|
| `raghilda.chunk` | `Chunk`, `MarkdownChunk`, `RetrievedChunk`, `Metric` |
| `raghilda.document` | `Document`, `MarkdownDocument` |
| `raghilda.embedding` | `EmbeddingProvider`, `EmbeddingOpenAI` |
| `raghilda.store` | `BaseStore`, `DuckDBStore`, `OpenAIStore` |
| `raghilda.chunker` | `BaseChunker`, `RaghildaMarkdownChunker`, `MarkdownChunk` |
| `raghilda.types` | `ChunkLike`, `DocumentLike`, `ChunkerLike`, `IntoChunk`, `IntoDocument` |
| `raghilda.read` | `read_as_markdown` |
| `raghilda.scrape` | `find_links` |

## Breaking changes

- `Store` renamed to `BaseStore`
- `EmbeddingProvider` and `EmbeddingOpenAI` now in `raghilda.embedding` (no longer re-exported from main package)
- `Chunk`, `Document`, `BaseChunker` moved to their respective domain modules

title: Handle bare carriage returns in Markdown chunking
description:
## Summary

`MarkdownChunker` now handles LF, CRLF, and bare carriage returns consistently when converting CommonMark source positions to character offsets. This prevents `IndexError` when chunking Markdown that contains bare carriage-return line endings.

Internally, source-position conversion and line-boundary snapping now share the same CommonMark-compatible line-start mapping. The public API is unchanged.

Public regression tests cover carriage returns before a paragraph, inside a paragraph, and as line-snapping boundaries.

Fixes #92.
